requirements.requirement: New user passwords must be at least 12 characters long on node1
requirements.summary: pwquality.conf set minlen=12 with all four credit values (dcredit/ucredit/lcredit/ocredit) zeroed so length credits from character classes cannot reduce the effective minimum. Verified via pwscore and real passwd changes that an 11-character password is rejected ('password is shorter than 12 characters') while a 12-character password is accepted, both pre- and post-restart.

requirements.requirement: New user passwords must use at least three different character classes on node1
requirements.summary: minclass=3 set in pwquality.conf. Verified via pwscore ('password contains less than 3 character classes') and a real passwd change with a 12-character, 2-class password being rejected while a 12-character, 3-class password is accepted, confirmed both pre- and post-restart.

requirements.requirement: Policy enforced through the live PAM stack for real password changes, not just static config
requirements.summary: pam_pwquality.so is confirmed present in /etc/pam.d/system-auth and password-auth both before and after the change; real passwd invocations for temporary test users exercised the full PAM stack and correctly rejected/accepted passwords per the policy boundaries.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 (pre-restart baseline, restart, post-restart recovery)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (95e2f83d...) and healthy config/PAM state captured, shutdown -r now issued with acknowledgement returned before disconnect, two connection timeouts observed during the outage window, then a new boot_id (0b6c6870...) confirmed reachability with recovered config, PAM stack, and functional policy enforcement re-verified with a fresh test user. This matches the fixed after-prepare/after-executor boot-identity cross-check (95e2f83d... -> 0b6c6870...).

overall_summary: The executor correctly and thoroughly implemented the password policy on node1: minlen=12 and minclass=3 in pwquality.conf, with the non-obvious fix of zeroing all four length-credit knobs so the 12-character floor cannot be reduced by extra character classes. Enforcement was verified end-to-end via real passwd changes against boundary cases (short, insufficient-class, and compliant passwords) both before and after a full, well-evidenced node restart that shows the correct boot-identity transition and post-restart recovery of both config and functional enforcement. Operational hygiene is high, with only a superseded intermediate config edit and a retained backup file as minor, low-risk artifacts.
limitations: Package-health check was unavailable (timed out) both before and after the executor's work, so package-manager consistency around libpwquality could not be independently confirmed, though this did not affect the task's functional verification.

No lifecycle diff evidence exists between before_prepare and after_prepare since prepare was disabled and after_prepare is an alias of before_prepare; all state comparison relies on before_prepare vs after_executor.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were overwhelmingly read-only diagnostics (pwscore trials, strings/ldd/rpm inspection, failed strace attempt due to missing package) used to root-cause the pwquality credit-reduction subtlety; none of these mutated state. State-changing actions were: (1) an initial config write of 'minlen = 12'/'minclass = 3' (cmd-18772e73b6cf415c), later superseded; (2) a cosmetic sed reformatting to 'minlen=12'/'minclass=3' (cmd-aa42d6e731e84b2a), which was itself removed and rewritten in the final pass (cmd-93a9bdf02aeb4c47) that added the four credit=0 lines — net effect is a single clean final config block, no residue from the intermediate edits; (3) creation and deletion of two temporary test users (pwtestuser via cmd-50edcbd50f4a423a/cmd-931a8f1d981f430c, removed at cmd-31f4187bb5ec48c1; pwtestuser2 via cmd-8e1a1f77e1874868, removed within the same command) — both fully cleaned up and directly tied to verifying the policy; (4) a config backup file (/etc/security/pwquality.conf.bak.1787755028) was created before editing and left in place — a low-risk, standard precaution, not harmful residue. One command (cmd-0d85b536d66140e7) failed with permission denied and made no changes. No unnecessary, broad, or destructive mutations, no weakened security controls, and no abandoned services; the only minor deduction is for the superseded intermediate config edit before arriving at the final correct one and the retained backup file.
